description:
Conditions represent exhaustion, frustration, maladies, or emotions that affect a PC as they adventure. They usually happen as a result of a Player's choices, and are rarely inflicted specifically upon you.  If **Marked** or **Locked** you have **dis** on its associated stat rolls.

Rare circumstances, such using certain magic items, may require a PC to mark a specific Condition. If they already have that Condition marked, they instead **lock it**. If it's already locked, then they mark another Condition of their choice.

Not only is the Condition active and affecting your character, but it won't clear under normal circumstances. Only effects that specify that they clear locked Conditions can do so, such as **Enjoy Downtime** or **Reveal Your Struggle**.
Cuts or bypasses thick armor and shielding. dmg of this type ignores armor and shield protection
Roll three dice (3d6) and ignore the lowest result, keeping the highest two.
Roll three dice (3d6) and ignore the highest result, keeping the lowest two.
Requires quick and careful aim to use well; Trade Blows+DEX (instead of +STR).
It needs ammunition to work. By default you always have enough, but you might run out as a result of a GM Move
Meant for a target a few paces away, close enough to see their face expressions but not to touch
Easy to hide from others unless they search you thoroughly
Meant for a target close enough to speak to, even if you may have to raise your voice
Meant for a target close enough to grab
Blessed by a divine power, and thus especially effective against a deity's enemies; adv on dmg rolls against them
Meant for a target close enough to speak to, even if you may have to raise your voice
After you use it, you need to spend time reloading, rearming, or recharging it to use it again
Needs two hands to use properly, maybe for weight, balance, a second part of it, etc.
Such as sturdy hides and padded gambesons, has DMG reduction 1 (to a minimum of 1) and it requires a minimum STR+1 to use properly.
Like a chain shirt, breastplate, or scale mail, has DMG reduction 2 (to a minimum of 1) and it requires a minimum STR+2 to use properly.
Like a proper chainmail or full plate, has DMG reduction 3 (to a minimum of 1) and it requires a minimum STR+2 to use properly.
Indicates how much damage a source does, they are d4, d6, d8, d10, d12 [ed: then maybe d8+d6 - like for MAG 4 spells?]

When a PC or NPC [has Resistance], they *Resist* it, meaning it's nearly useless against them. Resistance does not provide dmg reduction like armor does, but instead influences the **Fictional Positioning** and whether dmg (and Moves) would be rolled at all.

Overcoming such resistance usually requires imagination, special circumstances, or overwhelming power.
